title: Outlook: j/k step onto bundle rows
summary: Bundle rows are told apart from emails, so j/k lands on them, enter toggles them and a bundle of one gives way to its email.
plan: A reader meets the bundle row first, then moves through the list with the keyboard, then sees what happens when a bundle shrinks.
overview:
This PR fixes keyboard navigation in the Outlook list. The wrapper class bundle rows are recognised by was read from the wrong table, so they looked like emails.

1. **Bundle rows are told apart** (`bundle.js`, `email.js`)
2. **Keyboard walks the visible rows** (`keyboard.js`, `outlookUtils.js`)

4 files in 2 chapters.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Bundle rows are told apart
chapters.headline: A bundle row is now recognised as a bundle, and a bundle of one gives way to its email.
chapters.scenario: You open the inbox with a bundled label and a label with a single email.
chapters.summary: The wrapper class comes from the shared table, and bundle upkeep follows category changes.
chapters.answer: BUNDLE_WRAPPER_CLASS is read from CLASSES instead of OUTLOOK_CLASSES, so bundle rows are no longer mistaken for emails; a bundle of one is removed and an email that changes category follows its new bundle.
chapters.narrative:
### Chapter 1: Bundle rows are told apart

The scenario: you open the inbox with one bundled label and one label that has a single email.

1. The email class reads its wrapper class from [the shared table](ref:email-import), because the Outlook table never defined it. That is why bundle rows were never told apart from emails.
2. [The bundle upkeep](ref:bundle-sync) removes a leftover bundle row when only one email is left and shows the email in its natural place. A new bundle row starts collapsed and tucks away the emails that were already on show.
3. [The email side](ref:email-category) clears the old bundle's markers when a category changes and follows the new bundle's expanded state.

What to check: the three changes share one idea (a row knows which bundle it is in), so reading them together is easier than file by file.

One question worth asking: does a bundle of one still show when the bundle-one option is on? The text says it does not remove it then, which I would confirm in the options code.

Next is chapter 2, Keyboard walks the visible rows.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Keyboard walks the visible rows
chapters.headline: j and k step through every visible row in visual order, and enter and escape work on bundles.
chapters.scenario: You press j and k down the list, then enter on a bundle row and escape inside it.
chapters.summary: Navigation lands on bundle rows without toggling them; enter expands or collapses, escape collapses the selected email's bundle.
chapters.answer: Navigation walks all visible rows in visual order and highlights a bundle row it lands on; enter toggles it and escape collapses the bundle of the selected email; findReplacementRow keeps its same-bundle search for archive.
chapters.narrative:
### Chapter 2: Keyboard walks the visible rows

The scenario: you press j and k down the list, then enter on a bundle row and escape inside it.

1. [The key handlers](ref:keys) now walk every visible row in visual order. Landing on a bundle row highlights it and does not toggle it.
2. Enter on a bundle row expands or collapses it, and escape collapses the bundle of the selected email.
3. [visibleRows and findNextVisibleRow](ref:walk) in the utilities file are the walk the handlers use, with [the bundle helpers](ref:helpers) above them. [findReplacementRow](ref:walk) keeps its own same-bundle search, so an archive keeps the selection inside the bundle.

What to check: that archiving the last email of a bundle still selects something sensible.

What to raise: nothing blocking. Optional: a short comment on why findReplacementRow does not use the new walk.

That is the whole story; nothing is left to check beyond the archive case.
